gloss: to take seriously; to believe (something said in jest)

definitions.gloss: to take seriously; to believe; to take at face value
definitions.explanation: To treat something said — often a joke, exaggeration, or casual remark — as if it were genuinely meant. Frequently used when someone mistakenly believes something that was not intended seriously.

examples.japanese: {冗談|じょうだん}を{本気|ほんき}にするな。
{彼|かれ}は{私|わたし}の{嘘|うそ}を{本気|ほんき}にした。
{適当|てきとう}に{言|い}っただけなのに、{本気|ほんき}にしないでよ。
examples.english: I just said it offhandedly — don't take it seriously.

notes:
Composed of {本気|ほんき} (seriousness, earnestness) + にする (to treat as, to make into). The expression focuses on the listener's interpretation: treating something as serious or true.

USAGE:
Often used in the negative imperative {本気|ほんき}にするな / {本気|ほんき}にしないで (don't take it seriously). Distinct from {本気|ほんき}を{出|だ}す (to get serious, to give it one's all), which is about one's own effort rather than interpreting someone else's words.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {冗談|じょうだん}を{本気|ほんき}にする — to take a joke seriously
- {本気|ほんき}にしないで — don't take it seriously
- {本気|ほんき}にされる — to be taken seriously (passive)
- {嘘|うそ}を{本気|ほんき}にする — to believe a lie

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {真|ま}に{受|う}ける — to take at face value (very similar; slightly more formal)
- {信|しん}じる — to believe (neutral; broader usage)
- {本気|ほんき}を{出|だ}す — to get serious, to give it one's all (different meaning: about effort, not belief)
